data.body:
## Plan

I read the 11 deliveries `/webhooks/linear` has logged since JIM-128 (captured from the running server's pane). What they show:

* `actor` and `updatedFrom` are **top-level**, not inside `data`. `actor` is `{id, name, email, url, type}` and can be `null` (Linear sent a label update with no actor).
* `Issue` create/update/remove carry `data.identifier` (`JIM-130`). The claim foregent made on this issue is in the log: `actor.id = 442931c7…` with `updatedFrom = {updatedAt, sortOrder, startedAt, assigneeId, stateId}` — exactly the self-wake loop the mapper has to keep filterable.
* `IssueLabel` update carries the *label definition*, no issue anywhere. It is a real captured "payload with no issue".
* `updatedFrom` gives previous values as **raw ids** (`stateId: f6a28504…`), while `data` carries the resolved object (`data.state.name = "In Progress"`). So `state: Todo → Cancelled` is only half-reachable purely: the new side resolves to a name, the old side stays an id. I will not fabricate the old name with a lookup — the mapper stays pure.

### `linear.webhook_event(payload) -> Event | None`

Recognition, in order:

1. Not a dict, no string `type`, or no dict `data` → `None`. That is the envelope every entity delivery has, and it drops `AppUserNotification`-style payloads (which carry `notification`, not `data`) without guessing.
2. Issue key from `data.issue.identifier`, else `data.identifier`. Empty → `None`.
3. `type == "Comment"` → `EventKind.COMMENT`, body is `data.body`. Anything else → a new `EventKind.ISSUE_UPDATE`. Keying on "has an issue" rather than on a list of types means reactions, labels and attachments map the day they arrive, without a release to add them.
4. `actor.id` → `Event.actor`, `actor.name` → `Event.author`, both defaulting to `""` when the actor is null.

### The `ISSUE_UPDATE` body

One `field: old → new` line per entry in `updatedFrom`, where:

* a changed relation reported by id is shown under the name of the object it points at — `stateId` renders as `state`, taking the new value from `data.state.name`;
* `updatedAt`, `sortOrder` and `prioritySortOrder` are dropped. Linear rewrites all three on every issue write, and they bury the field a person actually changed.

So foregent's own claim reads:

```
state: f6a28504-0f21-49ad-b4f7-aa0940277df8 → In Progress
assignee: none → AJ
startedAt: none → 2026-08-19T19:19:27.117Z
```

### Also in this change

`EventKind`'s docstring says a Linear field update is deliberately not a wake, and `wake_message` has no case for one — an unhandled kind there leaves `header` unbound. Both are fixed, and `docs/PLAN.md` §5.1 records the reversal.

Mapping only: no route change, nothing delivered. One pull request's worth, in two commits (`events.py` gains the kind; `linear.py` gains the mapper).

### Test payloads

Tests run over the captured deliveries, held as fixtures. The log has no `Comment` yet, so I am generating one — this comment — and will capture it. It is written by foregent's own account, which makes it the acceptance criterion's "one written by foregent's own account" at the same time.

issue.title: Turn a Linear webhook delivery into a foregent event
